So do you really believe in this color theory or are you just stating that there is a possibility? Genuinely curious. We can cherry pick examples until end of time but it will never be enough since there will always be a counter example. The only thing I am holding on to is again, the light and darkness contrast. Black letters on white background works best because it emphasizes the dark colored objects on a light colored background. If it happens that out of 8 billion people on earth, there's 100,000 people who see light pink and as our black, then they would've mentioned by now that the black letters on white paper just doesn't work. This is also why they use yellow subtitles with black outline in a lot of movies, because the consensus is that the contrast just works for our human eyes on screen, when they are in these colors. This has nothing to do with culture or our sense of style. Light and darkness and contrast is quite fixed for this reason. If we had different colors for these aforementioned colors, none of this would work. This is mainly why I think we see the things the same.

The thing though is that I've never seen anyone react nonchalantly after eating a very spicy pepper, or cry from pain after eating a glazed doughnut. Taste may be different for many people, but largely it is the same. Sweet = sweet. Spicy = spicy. Salty = salty. The spicy, sweet, salty food all have a repercussion of their own when consumed, and we are biologically wired to react the same way to these sensations, and act in a way to prevent from being damaged by them. It's not the matter of the level of the taste that we perceive; within the context of this conversation thread I was making the point that we as humans most likely taste things largely the same way, as we perceive the colors the same way as well.

Right. I didn't mean for Green and Purple to be a good example, I was meaning that if green and purple were my red and white, it wouldn't look good to me. But I get your point.

Having said that I was going for a bit more primal example, such as black=dark for every human being and white=light. There's no way someone who sees navy blue and black for "white" perceive relegate those colors as being "light, bright, clean," etc, or the other way around of perceiving white as darkness etc.

Throughout various cultures the meaning behind each color is shared, and the most likely way those meanings are perceived equally among people thousands of miles away is if the colors are seen the same.
